2608.00402.title: DSETA: A Dual-Stage Continual Learning Framework for Travel Time Prediction in Dynamic Traffic Environments
2608.00402.paper_summary: Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) prediction is a core component of intelligent transportation systems. As traffic congestion patterns become increasingly dynamic in large cities, maintaining high prediction accuracy poses a major challenge for ride-hailing platforms. Existing methods either fail to adapt to irregular traffic patterns and sudden congestion, or suffer from new distributions without disentangling long-term trends from short-term fluctuations, thereby degrading model performance in real-world scenarios. To address this challenge, we propose DSETA, an incrementally updated Dual-Stage ETA prediction framework. Specifically, the continual learning process is divided into \textit{inter-day} and \textit{intra-day} stages. We first design the \textit{intra-day} learning stage, which relies entirely on real-time data to enable dynamic adaptation to short-term traffic patterns caused by events like holidays or accidents. Next, we develop the \textit{inter-day} learning stage, which leverages aggregated historical data from a short time window to capture knowledge of long-term distribution shifts, such as seasonal trends and traffic network evolution. Subsequently, to prevent catastrophic forgetting and preserve knowledge of regular patterns, we explore a \textit{Historical Traffic Knowledge Consolidation} module. Finally, we validate DSETA's effectiveness and robustness through extensive offline and online experiments conducted on real-world datasets from DiDi's platform. Online A/B tests across three major cities including Beijing, Wuhan, and Xi'an consistently demonstrated performance gains, achieving MAE reductions of 6.62\%, 0.73\%, and 2.40\% respectively. This framework has been successfully deployed in DiDi's production environment, processing hundreds of millions of daily requests and validating its strong performance in industrial applications.
2608.00402.paper_summary_zh: 預估到達時間（ETA）預測是智慧交通系統的核心組成部分。隨著大型城市的交通擁堵模式變得越來越動態，保持高預測準確性對於叫車平台來說是一個重大挑戰。現有的方法要麼無法適應不規則的交通模式和突發的擁堵，要麼在未能將長期趨勢與短期波動分開的情況下，受到新分佈的影響，從而降低了模型在現實場景中的性能。為了解決這一挑戰，我們提出了DSETA，一個增量更新的雙階段ETA預測框架。具體而言，持續學習過程被分為\textit{日間間隔}和\textit{日內}階段。我們首先設計了\textit{日內}學習階段，該階段完全依賴於實時數據，以便對由假期或事故等事件引起的短期交通模式進行動態適應。接下來，我們開發了\textit{日間間隔}學習階段，該階段利用來自短時間窗口的聚合歷史數據，以捕捉長期分佈變化的知識，例如季節性趨勢和交通網絡演變。隨後，為了防止災難性遺忘並保留對常規模式的知識，我們探索了一個\textit{歷史交通知識整合}模塊。最後，我們通過在DiDi平台的真實數據集上進行的大量離線和在線實驗，驗證了DSETA的有效性和穩健性。在包括北京、武漢和西安在內的三個主要城市進行的在線A/B測試一致顯示出性能提升，MAE分別減少了6.62\%、0.73\%和2.40\%。該框架已成功部署在DiDi的生產環境中，處理每天數億的請求，並驗證了其在工業應用中的強大性能。
